payload.task_text:
Our annual promotion cycle is coming up and I need to identify eligible candidates across the company. An employee is eligible for promotion if they have a performance rating of 4 or higher and at least 5 years of experience. Please pull this data from our data warehouse.

Create an Excel file called Promotion_Candidates.xlsx in the workspace with two sheets. The first sheet "By Department" should have columns Department, Eligible_Count, Avg_Salary rounded to 2 decimals, Avg_Experience rounded to 1 decimal, and Avg_Rating rounded to 2 decimals. Sort by Department alphabetically.

The second sheet "Summary" should have Metric and Value columns with Total_Eligible being the total count across all departments, Avg_Salary_Eligible as the weighted average salary of all eligible employees rounded to 2 decimals, and Avg_Experience_Eligible as the weighted average experience rounded to 1 decimal.

After creating the report, send an email to hr-director@company.com with subject "Promotion Cycle: Eligible Candidates Summary" that mentions the total number of eligible candidates and briefly describes the department with the highest count.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete it directly in the main agent; do not dispatch sub-agents. Freeze the task-visible agent-workspace absolute path from the Visible Boundary/current working directory. Run one set-based warehouse query using the literal predicate `performance_rating >= 4 AND years_of_experience >= 5`, returning each department's eligible count and raw salary/experience/rating aggregates plus company-wide aggregates. Compute the requested weighted summary from employee aggregates, not averages of department averages, and select the highest-count department deterministically.

From that one frozen result, create `<agent_workspace>/Promotion_Candidates.xlsx` with only the two exact sheets/headers/metrics in the task, alphabetical departments, literal values, and requested rounding; in the same native-parallel response send exactly one email to `hr-director@company.com` with subject `Promotion Cycle: Eligible Candidates Summary`. Read the two populated ranges back once, reconcile them to the query, and finish. Do not search Sent folders, retry folder aliases, read the sent message back, or add a verification wave.

nodes.text:
Query the company's Snowflake data warehouse to identify employees eligible for promotion under: performance rating >= 4 and years of experience >= 5. Determine the relevant database/schema/table(s) yourself. Return (1) department-level rows sorted alphabetically with Department, Eligible_Count, Avg_Salary rounded 2 decimals, Avg_Experience rounded 1 decimal, Avg_Rating rounded 2 decimals; (2) Total_Eligible; (3) weighted/global Avg_Salary_Eligible rounded 2 decimals and Avg_Experience_Eligible rounded 1 decimal; (4) department with highest eligible count, with deterministic handling/reporting of ties. Include the exact SQL used and key source table(s), and verify department counts sum to total. Read-only; do not create files or modify data. This is for an HR promotion review report.
Find eligible promotion data

Create `/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_gpt-5.6-sol/SingleUserTurn-sf-hr-promotion-review/workspace/Promotion_Candidates.xlsx` using the exact data below. It must contain exactly two sheets in this order if practical: `By Department` and `Summary`.

`By Department` columns: Department, Eligible_Count, Avg_Salary, Avg_Experience, Avg_Rating. Rows sorted alphabetically:
Engineering | 1424 | 60600.85 | 14.1 | 4.29
Finance | 1444 | 58930.16 | 13.9 | 4.29
HR | 1412 | 60658.10 | 14.4 | 4.31
Operations | 1371 | 58720.23 | 14.4 | 4.29
R&D | 1368 | 58410.80 | 14.5 | 4.28
Sales | 1432 | 60014.46 | 14.2 | 4.26
Support | 1363 | 60447.76 | 14.4 | 4.30

`Summary` columns: Metric, Value. Rows:
Total_Eligible | 9814
Avg_Salary_Eligible | 59688.45
Avg_Experience_Eligible | 14.3

Apply professional formatting: bold headers, sensible column widths, frozen header rows, autofilter/table if supported. Ensure salary cells display 2 decimals; department average experience displays 1 decimal; average ratings display 2 decimals; Summary Value formats should appropriately preserve 9814 as integer, 59688.45 as 2 decimals, and 14.3 as 1 decimal. Do not add extra data sheets. Verify the saved workbook by reading it back and report exact path, sheet names, ranges/values, and formatting verification. Do not alter any other files.
Build promotion workbook

Send an email to `hr-director@company.com` with subject exactly `Promotion Cycle: Eligible Candidates Summary`. The body should be concise and professional, stating that 9,814 employees meet the promotion eligibility criteria (performance rating of 4 or higher and at least 5 years of experience). Briefly describe the department with the highest count: Finance has the highest number with 1,444 eligible employees, representing approximately 14.7% of all eligible candidates. Mention that the attached report provides department-level averages and overall summary. Attach `/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_gpt-5.6-sol/SingleUserTurn-sf-hr-promotion-review/workspace/Promotion_Candidates.xlsx`. Verify the send result and return recipient, subject, attachment, and message/send ID if available. Do not send any other email.
